hypothesis: Dynamic 16-pixel chunks may improve load balance over the measured dynamic-64 schedule when per-pixel hit and ambient-occlusion work varies, especially at high thread counts, but the extra scheduling overhead may offset that benefit. A direct serial path should avoid OpenMP team overhead at one thread. This tests chunk granularity against the valid dynamic-64 candidate; observed aggregate timings do not establish a per-configuration winner.
notes: This candidate changes the dynamic pixel chunk size to 16 while preserving a serial one-thread path and using no more than the requested thread count. Per-pixel SplitMix64 streams are keyed by linear pixel index; workers write only that pixel's output triplet. The controller must establish correctness and repeated timings for every official configuration; no new performance result is claimed.
transformations: Replace ambient-worker drand48 calls with per-pixel SplitMix64 streams seeded from a serial render-seed draw and linear pixel index.
Use OpenMP dynamic scheduling over flattened pixels with chunk size 16 and num_threads capped at the requested thread count; use a direct serial loop for one thread.
Preserve the primary-ray and ambient-ray counts, ray calculations, and one-pixel-per-worker output ownership.
